title: My first issue
Phase 1: Pare down br to simple agent-compatible team tracker
description:
Fork-based simplification of br into a clean team issue tracker. Target use: human-primary teams where each developer has a per-dev AI agent handling task updates and sync bookkeeping. CRDT peer-to-peer sync planned as future transport layer; br emits and reads issues.jsonl as its i/o surface.

Key design decisions from planning session:
- Sync model: flush (DB->JSONL) + dirty-preserving import (JSONL->DB). Conflict = hard stop.
- No 3-way merge: export_hashes table serves as per-issue base for conflict detection.
- Status set: Open, InProgress, Draft, Deferred, Closed, Tombstone
- Dep types: blocks, parent-child, related, duplicates
- Issue body: description only (cut design/AC/notes)
- IDs: keep hash-based (conflict-free for CRDT)
- Output: keep rich_rust + JSON, cut toon_rust
- MCP: keep as feature flag
- TUI: phase 2 (full editor, ratatui+crossterm); phase 1 must keep storage layer clean and separate from CLI formatting
close_reason: Duplicate of beads_rust-dgi — created by a failed first attempt

title: Rewrite sync engine: dirty-preserving import, cut 3-way merge and witness system
description:
Replace the 3-way merge sync engine with a simpler dirty-preserving import. The CRDT sync layer (external, future) owns conflict resolution between peers; br only needs to protect local unflushed work during import.

CUT ENTIRELY:
- src/sync/witness.rs (~1,894 lines) — Merkle JSONL witnesses, not wired to flush/import paths
- src/sync/history.rs (~1,375 lines) — local snapshot management; git history is the recovery path
- .beads/beads.base.jsonl — common ancestor for 3-way merge; no longer needed
- Three-way merge engine in sync/mod.rs: three_way_merge(), merge_issue(), MergeContext, MergeReport, ConflictType, ConflictResolution, MergeResult, load_base_snapshot(), save_base_snapshot*() (~400 lines)
- 4-phase collision detection in sync/mod.rs (lines ~3680-4424, ~1,900 lines) — replace with simple upsert
- Tombstone preservation helpers (only needed for --rebuild mode, which is cut)
- Staleness/witness tracking: compute_staleness(), auto_import_probe_refreshing_witnesses(), etc.
- sync/mod.rs: compute_staleness_refreshing_witnesses(), build_base_witness_artifacts()

CUT SYNC MODES from src/cli/commands/sync.rs:
- execute_merge() — three-way merge mode
- execute_status() — staleness/witness-based status (separate from basic import/export)
- execute_witness() + build_witness_for_path() — witness computation
- maybe_delegate_rebuild() — rebuild/reset mode

KEEP:
- --flush-only: DB -> JSONL export (unchanged from current)
- --import-only: JSONL -> DB (rewritten with new logic below)

NEW IMPORT LOGIC (replaces 4-phase collision detection):
Algorithm:
  1. Check for conflict markers in JSONL (keep existing ensure_no_conflict_markers())
  2. Parse all issues from JSONL (keep read_issues_from_jsonl())
  3. Get dirty issue IDs + marked_at from dirty_issues table (get_dirty_issue_metadata())
  4. For each issue in incoming JSONL:
     a. If issue_id is in dirty_issues AND incoming content_hash != export_hashes[issue_id].content_hash:
        -> CONFLICT: add to conflict_list with {id, local_version, remote_version}
     b. If issue_id is in dirty_issues AND hashes match (peer didn't change it):
        -> Skip (local DB wins)
     c. Otherwise: upsert from JSONL (remote wins)
     d. New issues (not in DB): insert directly
  5. If conflict_list is non-empty: rollback, return hard error with full conflict report
     Error format: {conflicts: [{id, title, local_updated_at, remote_updated_at}], message: 'Flush first to include your local changes, then re-import'}
  6. Otherwise: commit, update export_hashes for all imported issues, update metadata['last_import_time']

Key tables used (all already exist):
- dirty_issues: which issues have unflushed local changes
- export_hashes: content_hash at last flush (serves as per-issue 'base' without beads.base.jsonl)

title: Add minimal br check command (replaces doctor)
description:

THREE CHECKS:
1. Conflict marker detection

   - Checks issues.jsonl for <<<<<<</=======/>>>>>>> git conflict markers
   - Error: 'Resolve git merge conflicts in issues.jsonl before syncing'

2. Schema version check
   - Query: SELECT value FROM metadata WHERE key = 'schema_version'
   - Compare against current expected schema version constant
   - Warn if mismatch: 'Schema version X found, expected Y. Run br sync --import-only to migrate.'

3. Lock file staleness check
   - stat .beads/.write.lock and .beads/.sync.lock
   - Warn if mtime > 1 hour: 'Stale lock file detected at PATH (age: Xm). May indicate a crashed process.'

OUTPUT FORMAT (--json):
{
  'status': 'ok' | 'warn' | 'error',
  'checks': [
    {'name': 'conflict_markers', 'status': 'ok'|'warn'|'error', 'message': '...'},
    {'name': 'schema_version', 'status': 'ok'|'warn'|'error', 'message': '...'},
    {'name': 'lock_files', 'status': 'ok'|'warn'|'error', 'message': '...'}

}

Exit codes: 0=all ok, 1=at least one warn, 2=at least one error

title: Get my head around the repo structure
Phase 1 (alt): Greenfield rewrite of br on rusqlite
description:
Alternative to beads_rust-dgi (refactor-in-place). Verdict: greenfield + rusqlite is faster than refactoring the existing codebase and then swapping fsqlite, because the plan already deletes or rewrites the two biggest fsqlite-contaminated files (doctor.rs 19K lines cut, sync/mod.rs 9K lines rewritten), leaving sqlite.rs (21K lines) as the only remaining fsqlite file — but 70%+ of its content is fsqlite-specific boilerplate (290 API calls, 880 SqliteValue usages, 20+ bug workarounds) that is simply deleted in a greenfield approach.

APPROACH
- New crate, clean Cargo.toml with rusqlite replacing all 15 fsqlite-* crates
- Cherry-pick from existing impl: SQL schema (verbatim), SQL query strings, dependency graph traversal, content hashing (SHA-256), JSONL dedup logic, Issue model (simplified per dgi.4 spec)
- Write rusqlite calling convention once, cleanly — no workarounds, no FK suppression, no per-row insert loops, no custom execute_batch lexer
- Implement only the commands being kept (per dgi.6 cut list)
- Storage trait abstraction from day one (missing in current impl) so backend is swappable

WHAT IS REUSED (verbatim or near-verbatim)
- SQLite schema DDL (standard SQL, fully portable)
- SQL query strings from sqlite.rs
- Dependency graph traversal algorithms
- SHA-256 content hashing and hash-based short ID generation
- JSONL import/export logic (simplified sync engine)
- Issue, Dependency, Comment, Event, Label model types (simplified)
- CLI command logic for kept commands
- rich_rust output formatting
- MCP server (opt-in feature flag)

WHAT IS DISCARDED
- All 21 fsqlite bug workarounds (PRAGMA foreign_keys OFF/ON, per-row insert loops, 370-line execute_batch lexer, ORDER BY sort-in-Rust, quarantine_truncated_wal_sidecar, etc.)
- The 880 SqliteValue usages and 290 fsqlite API call sites
- All 15 fsqlite-* crate dependencies
- doctor.rs (19K lines), orphans, changelog, lint, query, history commands
- 3-way merge and witness system from sync engine
- toon_rust dependency and TOON output format
- self_update feature flag
- Go-parity conformance tests (beads_rust is no longer a Go bd port)
- write_combining, policy, cache, inheritance, close_policy, coordination modules
- Fields cut per dgi.4: estimated_minutes, agent_context, closed_by_session, sender, ephemeral, is_template, pinned, source_system, source_repo, source_repo_path, compaction group

RISKS
- Implicit behavior loss: dependency graph correctness, JSONL dedup edge cases — mitigate by porting those algorithms deliberately with unit tests
- Scope creep: strict feature gate at the kept-commands list
- Test coverage: greenfield has no existing tests to validate against — mitigate by writing tests alongside each module

STATUS: Planning. Replaces beads_rust-dgi if adopted. Both epics kept open until decision made.

title: Storage layer: rusqlite SQLite backend implementing Storage trait

Schema: port DDL verbatim (tables: issues, dependencies, comments, events, labels, label_memberships, export_hashes, blocked_issues_cache). Simplify: drop columns cut in model stage.

rusqlite calling convention (write once, use everywhere):
- Connection::open() / open_with_flags() for read-only
- conn.execute(sql, params![...]) for mutations
- conn.query_row(sql, params![...], |row| ...) for single-row queries  
- conn.prepare(sql)?.query_map(params![...], |row| ...)?.collect() for multi-row
- conn.transaction()? RAII guard — no manual BEGIN/COMMIT strings
- conn.execute_batch(sql) — built-in, replaces the 370-line custom lexer in legacy

DELETED workarounds (none needed):
- No PRAGMA foreign_keys OFF/ON wrapping every mutation
- No per-row insert loops (bulk INSERT works correctly)
- No ORDER BY sort-in-Rust (rusqlite honors it)
- No busy_timeout hot-spin workaround (use conn.busy_timeout())
- No WAL quarantine logic
- No custom execute_batch SQL lexer

Port algorithms deliberately with unit tests:
- Dependency graph traversal (ready query, blocked query, cycle detection)
- Filtered list queries (status, priority, assignee, label)
- Search (full-text across title + description)
- Event log append and retrieval

title: Sync engine: simplified flush + dirty-preserving import
description:
Rewrite the sync engine from scratch in src/sync/. The existing legacy/src/sync/mod.rs (9,423 lines) is being replaced, not ported — most of its size is the 3-way merge and witness system, which is cut entirely.

Target behavior (per beads_rust-dgi.5 spec):
- Flush (DB→JSONL): serialize all non-tombstone issues to .beads/issues.jsonl, sorted by id. Atomic write (temp file + rename). No git operations.
- Import (JSONL→DB): dirty-preserving — issues present in JSONL but not in DB are inserted; issues present in both are merged by updated_at (newest wins); issues in DB but not JSONL are left untouched (no deletion). Conflict = hard stop with clear error message.
- export_hashes table: serves as per-issue base for dirty detection (was the local version modified since last flush?)
- .beads/ path discovery: port from legacy/src/sync/path.rs (walk up directory tree)

JSONL dedup logic to port verbatim from legacy with unit tests:
- SHA-256 content dedup across sync boundaries
- Tombstone propagation

Cut entirely:
- 3-way merge system
- Witness / snapshot history system (legacy/src/sync/history.rs)
- WAL quarantine / VACUUM INTO compaction 
- All fsqlite-specific connection lifecycle management
